List the indicators bdhs can compute

Source: R/indicators.R
bdhs_indicator_list.Rd

Returns the registry of indicators that bdhs_estimate(), bdhs_add_indicators() and bdhs_validate() understand: what each one measures, which recode file it is computed from, the denominator rules, the matching DHS Program API indicator and the survey rounds it supports.

Usage

bdhs_indicator_list(topic = NULL, recode = NULL)

Arguments

topic

Optional topic(s) to keep, e.g. "family_planning", "maternal_health", "child_health", "nutrition". Matching is case-insensitive.

recode

Optional recode code(s) ("IR", "KR", "BR", "PR", ...) to keep only indicators computed from those files.

Value

A tibble with one row per indicator and columns id, label, topic, recode, type ("proportion", "mean", "median" or "rate"), api_id, all_women (all-woman factor used for all-women denominators, or NA), window (reference period in months, if any), rounds and validated (list columns of survey ids), definition, notes and reference.

Details

Definitions follow the Guide to DHS Statistics and port the logic of the DHS Program's DHS-Indicators-R code (https://github.com/DHSProgram/DHS-Indicators-R), adapted to the Bangladesh questionnaires (for example the country-specific list of medically trained providers, which changes between rounds, and the 2022 long/short women's questionnaire design). The validated column lists the rounds for which the package's computation was checked against the official DHS value with the maintainer's copy of the microdata.

Examples

bdhs_indicator_list()
#> # A tibble: 97 × 13
#>    id          label topic recode type  api_id all_women window rounds validated
#>    <chr>       <chr> <chr> <chr>  <chr> <chr>  <chr>      <int> <list> <list>   
#>  1 fp_cpr_any  Cont… fami… IR     prop… FP_CU… NA            NA <chr>  <chr [2]>
#>  2 fp_cpr_mod… Cont… fami… IR     prop… FP_CU… NA            NA <chr>  <chr [2]>
#>  3 fp_cpr_tra… Cont… fami… IR     prop… FP_CU… NA            NA <chr>  <chr [2]>
#>  4 fp_method_… Marr… fami… IR     prop… FP_CU… NA            NA <chr>  <chr [2]>
#>  5 fp_method_… Marr… fami… IR     prop… FP_CU… NA            NA <chr>  <chr [2]>
#>  6 fp_method_… Marr… fami… IR     prop… FP_CU… NA            NA <chr>  <chr [2]>
